sentences: Build and deploy application backends.
Add authentication, PostgreSQL/MySQL databases, vector databases, storage, serverless functions, realtime, messaging, hosting, domains, CDN and firewall.

Databases: TablesDB (relational tables, rows, columns, indexes, relationships, transactions), DocumentsDB (schemaless JSON collections and documents), and VectorsDB (vector embeddings with similarity search, plus a text embeddings API).
Dedicated databases: managed PostgreSQL, MySQL and MongoDB with direct connections, backups, branches, replicas, connection pooling, point-in-time recovery and extensions such as pgvector.
Auth: users, sessions, teams, labels, MFA, OAuth2 providers, tokens, presences for who is online, and an OAuth2/OIDC server so the project can act as an identity provider.
Storage: buckets and files with image previews and transformations.
Functions: serverless functions across many runtimes with Git or manual deployments, executions, schedules and environment variables.
Sites: host static and server-rendered web apps.
Messaging: email, SMS and push notifications through providers, topics and targets.
Network: custom domains, CDN cache invalidation and proxy rules, and Firewall rules that deny, challenge, rate limit, redirect or bypass traffic to the API, Functions and Sites.
Domains: register, transfer and renew domains and manage DNS records.
Operations: project backups and restores, migrations from other platforms, webhooks, usage metrics, and Advisor reports with insights.

This local Appwrite MCP connection uses the API key, endpoint, and project configured in the server environment.
Appwrite API calls target that configured APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID by default.
You authenticate against the Appwrite console, which can list your organizations and projects but stores no project data itself.

Project-scoped tools (every database type, users, teams, storage, functions, sites, messaging, firewall, advisor) need a target project: use appwrite_get_context first, then pass the selected project id as project_id to appwrite_call_tool.
Organization-scoped console tools (e.g. creating a project or managing domains) need organization_id.

File/image uploads: pass a public URL as the file argument (e.g. {"url": "https://..."}) so the server downloads it directly; for very small files you may pass inline base64 ({"filename": ..., "content": ..., "encoding": "base64"}).
For questions about Appwrite concepts, products, features, or guides, use appwrite_search_docs — it searches the official Appwrite documentation and needs no project or credentials.
Appwrite workflow: use appwrite_get_context to understand the current connection and available project resources, then use appwrite_search_tools and appwrite_call_tool for specific operations.
Mutating hidden tools require confirm_write=true.
Large results are stored as resources; read the URI returned by the tool.
Hosted HTTP returns tool results inline, including images and other binary payloads.
